packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification, author, work or earlier reading for this leaf. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg to image-014.jpg (plus one file-name listing of the packet folder to learn the image names; packet.json was not opened). No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

Conventions: (..) = proposed expansion; ?word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = not readable by me in these tiles; line numbers are counted from the top of the named image, counting partly cropped lines. The script is a small, fast, heavily abbreviated cursive; the tiles are low in pixel size relative to the letter size, so MOST readings below are tentative even where no question mark is given. Treat single words as checkable only where I say "clear".

------------------------------------------------------------
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
------------------------------------------------------------
Two faces of one small leaf/fragment (about 10 cm wide by 16 cm high by the ruler), upright orientation.

Face 1: overview image-001; tiles image-002 (upper left), image-003 (upper right), image-004 (middle left), image-005 (middle right), image-006 (lower left), image-007 (lower right).
Face 2: overview image-008; tiles image-009 (upper left), image-010 (upper right), image-011 (middle left), image-012 (middle right), image-013 (lower left), image-014 (lower right).

- Two columns on each face, roughly 38-40 lines per column on face 2. Narrow intercolumn. Top line of each column is cut through or sits on the edge (leaf trimmed at top); bottom margin survives (blank strip below the last lines).
- No running title, no rubric and no coloured paraph seen in the cursive text. No underlining seen. No interlinear gloss seen, apart from one or two small superscript insertions (noted below). No marginal notes seen.
- Face 1 is badly abraded/soiled; the right column is almost entirely lost to the eye. Face 2 is far better.
- Face 1, right column, lower third (image-005 bottom, image-007 top): one line of large formal book script (textura-type minims in black, on a yellowish wash) preceded by a large red initial, cut by the right edge. It reads as a red "A" (or a round "Q"/"a"-shaped initial) followed by minims, "?mun?" / "?nun?" / "?mini?" - only minims survive before the edge. It is in a different script, size and ink from the cursive text. Tentative interpretation only: either a display heading/lemma, or offset/underlying writing from another leaf. I cannot decide from the images.
- Small brownish wax-like or slip-like marks are scattered over both faces (they look like tiny oblong stains, not writing). Several holes (binding/nail holes) near the corners and the left edge; horizontal tears at the left edge (face 2) / right edge (face 1), showing the two faces are back to back.
- Tentative interpretation: continuous scholastic prose, not verse and not main-text-plus-gloss. The recurring formula read on face 2 ("... inquantum tractatur in tradicione libri ...") suggests a passage distinguishing how one subject is treated in several books; I do not infer which.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. AREAS SELECTED / AREAS LEFT UNREAD
------------------------------------------------------------
Selected: face 2 right column (best preserved; image-010, -012, -014), face 2 left column (image-009, -011, -013), face 1 left column (image-002, -004, -006).
Essentially unread: face 1 right column (image-003, -005, -007) - only isolated strokes; face 1 left column middle (image-002 lines 14 ff., image-004 lines 1-7).
A raking-light, UV or higher-resolution capture of face 1 would be needed; for face 2 a tile at roughly twice the pixel density would settle most of the question marks.

------------------------------------------------------------
3. FACE 2, RIGHT COLUMN (image-010, image-012, image-014)
------------------------------------------------------------

Fairly secure in this column: the repeated frame "Jnquantum tractatur in tradicione libri", "sed inquantum tractatur", "ut dicunt quidam", "Et ex quo omnia ista", "siue", "de quocumque ordine de quo". The book names after "libri" are abbreviated and I could not read any of them with confidence; I record the candidates only as what the letter shapes allow, not as an identification.

7. LIMITATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------
- This is an unverified image reading. The hand is a compressed cursive with many suspensions; at the supplied tile resolution individual letters are a few pixels wide, so the transcription is mostly at the level of word shapes plus recognisable abbreviation marks. Question marks are meant literally.
- Top line of every column is cut. Left edge of face 2 left column loses initial letters. Face 1 right column and the middle of face 1 left column are effectively unread because of abrasion, not for want of looking at the tiles.
- Column order within each face (left then right) is assumed, not proven; which face is recto is not determinable from the images.
- Line counts per tile include partly cropped lines at the tile top; adjacent tiles overlap by three to four lines, flagged above.
- I did not attempt to identify the work or author and supplied no words from memory of any text. I did nothing beyond the stated rules other than the single file-name listing mentioned at the top.
